examples.en: Curly perms are back in fashion these days.

examples.ko: 제 머리는 비가 오면 더 곱슬곱슬해져요.
examples.en: My hair gets curlier when it rains.
The baby's hair is curly and so cute.
After getting a curly perm, I look softer.
This puppy has curly fur.
I went to the salon to straighten my curly hair.

explain: 머리카락이나 강아지 털처럼 가늘게 말려 있는 것에 써요. 반대로 곧은 머리는 '생머리'라고 해요. 활용은 '곱슬곱슬해요', '곱슬곱슬한'이에요.

phrases.en: I want to straighten my curly hair.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ' 형태로 뒤의 명사를 꾸며 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '-ㄴ' form modifies the noun that follows.

phrases.example: 저는 곱슬머리라서 아침마다 머리 손질이 힘들어요.
phrases.en: I have curly hair, so styling it every morning is hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 곱슬곱슬한 머리를 한 단어로 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is a single word for curly hair.

phrases.en: My hair isn't curly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 곱슬이 아닐 때는 이렇게 부정으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use the negative form to say hair is not curly.

explain_en: It is used for things that curl finely, like hair or a dog's fur. Straight hair is called '생머리'. It conjugates as '곱슬곱슬해요' and '곱슬곱슬한'.

examples.en: I played all summer, so my face became tanned.
My younger sibling has dark skin and looks healthy.
Her white teeth look pretty against her dark skin.
My arms are dark from being in the sun.
Her skin is dark, but her face is clear and pretty.
Children with deeply tanned skin are playing on the beach.

explain: 주로 사람의 피부가 약간 검은 모습을 말해요. '가무잡잡하다'와 비슷한 말이고, '거무스름하다'보다 피부에 쓸 때가 더 많아요. 칭찬이 될 때도 있지만 상대에 따라 조심해서 써요.

phrases.en: My younger sibling has a dark complexion.
phrases.nuance_ko: 거의 같은 뜻이고 조금 더 가벼운 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same meaning with a slightly lighter feel.

phrases.en: A dark-skinned child came running over, smiling.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람 앞에서 꾸밀 때 쓰는 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form used to describe a person.

phrases.en: In winter my skin is not very dark.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아니라고 말할 때 쓰는 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form.

explain_en: It mainly describes skin that is somewhat dark. It is similar to '가무잡잡하다', and compared with '거무스름하다' it is more often used for skin. It can sound like a compliment, but use it carefully depending on the person.

examples.ko: 이 몸뚱이로는 무거운 짐을 못 들겠어요.
examples.en: With this body of mine, I can't carry heavy loads.

examples.ko: 하루 종일 누워 있었더니 몸뚱이가 무거워요.
examples.en: I lay around all day, and my body feels heavy.

examples.ko: 뱀은 머리는 작은데 몸뚱이는 아주 길어요.
examples.en: A snake has a small head but a very long body.

examples.ko: 눈사람은 큰 몸뚱이에 작은 얼굴을 달았어요.
examples.en: The snowman has a big body with a small face.

examples.ko: 이 몸뚱이 하나 믿고 여기까지 왔어요.
examples.en: I got this far trusting just this one body of mine.

examples.ko: 할아버지는 낡은 몸뚱이를 이끌고 시장에 가세요.
examples.en: My grandfather drags his worn-out body to the market.

explain: '몸'보다 거칠고 가벼운 느낌이어서 다른 사람 몸에는 쓰지 않는 게 좋아요. '이 몸뚱이'처럼 자기 몸을 낮추거나 힘들다고 말할 때, 동물이나 물건의 몸통을 말할 때 써요.

phrases.en: I worked hard relying only on my own body.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가진 것이 몸밖에 없다는 뜻으로 자기 몸을 낮춰 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Humbly says one's body is all one has.

phrases.en: I'm so tired my body won't listen to me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸이 마음대로 움직이지 않을 때 가볍게 투덜거리는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual grumble when your body won't move as you want.

phrases.example: 풀 사이로 뱀의 긴 몸뚱이가 보였어요.
phrases.en: I saw the snake's long body between the grass.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동물의 몸통을 거칠게 말할 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also used roughly for an animal's body.

explain_en: It is rougher and less polite than 몸, so avoid using it for another person's body. You use it for your own body when you are being self-deprecating or tired, as in 이 몸뚱이, and for the trunk of an animal or object.

dis.h: blunt, rough word; whole body or torso
gh: everyday word; body or physical condition
formal; body in check-ups and measurements
literary; flesh body, contrasted with soul

p.n: The swap is neutral; the original is blunt and stresses the bulk of the body.

t90.ax: The snowman has a big body with a small face.

examples.en: Grandfather's hair has turned white, but he is very healthy.
A white-haired grandmother got on the bus.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 백발로 염색하고 새 영화에 나왔어요.
examples.en: The actor dyed his hair white and appeared in the new movie.
He had white hair and wore glasses.
I dyed my hair to hide the gray.
The professor with a head of white hair began the lecture.

explain: 머리 전체가 하얗게 센 모습은 '백발'이라고 해요. 몇 가닥만 센 것은 '흰머리'라고 하고, 젊은 나이에 센 머리카락은 '새치'라고 따로 불러요. 보통 나이 드신 분의 모습을 말할 때 많이 써요.

phrases.en: My father has a lot more gray hair now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몇 가닥만 센 머리도 말할 수 있어서 '백발'보다 가볍게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can refer to just a few gray strands, so it's lighter than 백발.

phrases.en: I worried so much that my hair turned white.
phrases.nuance_ko: 머리카락 색이 변하는 과정을 동사로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses a verb to describe hair changing color.

phrases.en: I'm only twenty, but I already have some gray hairs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 젊은 나이에 난 흰 머리카락을 말해요. 나이 든 분께는 안 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gray hairs that appear at a young age; not used for older people.

explain_en: 백발 is a whole head of white hair. A few white strands are 흰머리, and gray hairs that appear at a young age are called 새치. It is mostly used when describing older people.

t90.ax: I dyed my hair to hide the gray.

examples.en: A velvet sofa feels very soft to the touch.

examples.ko: 그녀는 파란 벨벳 드레스를 입고 나왔어요.
examples.en: She came out wearing a blue velvet dress.

examples.ko: 극장 의자는 빨간 벨벳으로 덮여 있어요.
examples.en: The theater seats are covered in red velvet.
Velvet dresses are popular in winter.

examples.ko: 이 상자 안은 검은 벨벳으로 되어 있어요.
examples.en: The inside of this box is made of black velvet.
Thanks to the velvet curtains, the room is dark.

explain: 벨벳은 겉이 보들보들하고 부드러운 천이에요. 같은 천을 '비로드'라고도 불러요. '벨벳 케이크'처럼 음식 이름에도 붙어요.

phrases.en: My grandmother treasures her velvet skirt.
phrases.nuance_ko: 벨벳과 같은 천을 부르는 말이에요. 나이 드신 분들이 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Another name for the same fabric as 벨벳, used more often by older people.

phrases.en: I hung velvet curtains in the living room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 벨벳은 소파, 드레스, 커튼 같은 물건 앞에 붙여서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 벨벳 is often placed before items such as sofas, dresses and curtains.

phrases.en: This cat's fur is as soft as velvet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아주 부드러운 느낌을 비유할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as a comparison to describe something very soft.

explain_en: 벨벳 is a fabric with a soft, plush surface. The same fabric is also called 비로드. It also appears in food names, as in 벨벳 케이크 (red velvet cake).

en: bulging; protrudingly in a rounded way

examples.en: His belly is sticking out round.

examples.ko: 다람쥐가 입에 먹이를 넣어 볼을 볼록 부풀렸어요.
examples.en: The squirrel stuffed food in its mouth and puffed out its cheeks.
The balloon swelled up round.
Your pocket is bulging out.

examples.ko: 이불 속에서 고양이 등이 볼록 올라왔어요.
examples.en: A cat's back rose up in a round bump under the blanket.

examples.ko: 아이가 가방을 볼록 채워서 학교에 갔어요.
examples.en: The child went to school with a bulging bag.

explain: 볼록은 둥글게 살짝 튀어나온 모양에 써요. 더 크고 많이 튀어나오면 '불룩'을 쓰는데 느낌이 더 커요. 반대로 안쪽으로 들어간 모양은 '오목'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: The pocket bulges out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 둥글게 살짝 나온 모양을 '튀어나오다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Combined with '튀어나오다' for a slightly rounded bulge.

phrases.en: A bump rose up on my forehead.
phrases.nuance_ko: 표면 위로 둥글게 솟는 모양에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for something rising roundly above the surface.

phrases.en: I sat on a spot where the ground rises slightly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 땅이나 바닥이 조금 높게 올라온 모양을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes ground that rises up slightly.

explain_en: 볼록 describes a slight, round bulge. For something bigger and more swollen, Koreans use '불룩', which feels stronger. The opposite, a dent going inward, is '오목'.

examples.en: I had an X-ray exam at the hospital.

examples.ko: 엑스선으로 찍으면 뼈 상태를 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: With an X-ray, you can see the condition of the bones.

examples.ko: 엑스선은 눈에 보이지 않지만 몸을 통과해요.
examples.en: X-rays are invisible, but they pass through the body.
At the airport, you put your bag through an X-ray machine.

examples.ko: 엑스선 사진을 보니 다행히 부러지지 않았대요.
examples.en: The X-ray picture shows that, luckily, it isn't broken.
At the dentist, they took an X-ray and checked for cavities.

explain: 병원에서는 '엑스레이'라는 말을 더 많이 써요. 사진은 '엑스레이 사진', 찍는 것은 '엑스레이를 찍다'라고 해요. '엑스선'은 그 빛(전자기파)의 이름이라 설명문이나 뉴스에서 자주 보여요.

phrases.en: I had an X-ray taken at the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: '엑스선'과 같은 말인데, 병원이나 일상 대화에서는 '엑스레이'를 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same thing as 엑스선, but 엑스레이 is more common at the hospital and in daily talk.

phrases.en: My leg hurt, so I had an X-ray exam.
phrases.nuance_ko: '검사를 받다'와 함께 병원에서 몸을 살펴볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 검사를 받다 when the body is examined at a hospital.

phrases.en: You can see the bones well in the X-ray picture.
phrases.nuance_ko: 찍어 놓은 사진 자체를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the finished picture itself.

explain_en: At hospitals people more often say '엑스레이'. The image is called '엑스레이 사진' and taking one is '엑스레이를 찍다'. '엑스선' is the name of the ray itself, so it appears more in explanations and the news.

t90.ax: I had an X-ray exam at the hospital.

examples.ko: 잠을 못 자면 병에 대한 저항력이 떨어져요.
examples.en: If you can't sleep, your resistance to illness drops.
Exercise is important to build up resistance.
Resistance gets weaker as you get older.
Does taking vitamins help your resistance?

examples.ko: 몸의 저항력 덕분에 독감에도 가볍게 지나갔어요.
examples.en: Thanks to my body's resistance, even the flu passed lightly.
I chose a plant that resists the cold well.

explain: 병이나 추위, 스트레스 같은 나쁜 영향에 맞서 버티는 힘이에요. 몸의 병뿐 아니라 추위나 충격에 버티는 힘에도 써요. 병에 대해서는 '면역력'이라고 더 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: Children have weak resistance to colds.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병에 잘 걸리는 상태를 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a state in which one gets sick easily.

phrases.example: 비타민을 먹으면 저항력을 높일 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Taking vitamins can raise your resistance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸을 더 튼튼하게 만든다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means making the body stronger.

phrases.en: My immunity is low, so I often get sick.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병에 대해서는 '저항력'보다 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used more often than 저항력 when talking about illness.

explain_en: It is the strength to withstand bad influences such as illness, cold or stress. It is used not just for disease but also for resisting cold or shock. For illness, people more often say '면역력'.

t90.ax: Resistance gets weaker as you get older.

examples.en: My face burned with embarrassment.

examples.ko: 매운 고추를 씹자 입안이 화끈 불붙은 것 같았어요.
examples.en: When I bit into a hot pepper, my mouth felt like it was on fire.

examples.ko: 뜨거운 물이 닿자 손이 화끈 아팠어요.
examples.en: When hot water touched it, my hand stung hotly.
My forehead feels burning hot, maybe from a cold.

examples.ko: 민망한 말을 듣고 귀까지 화끈 뜨거워졌어요.
examples.en: After hearing that embarrassing remark, even my ears flushed hot.
I put a heat pack on in midwinter, and my stomach felt hot.

explain: 몸의 한 곳이 갑자기 뜨거워지는 느낌을 나타내는 의태어예요. 부끄러울 때 '얼굴이 화끈거리다', 매운 걸 먹은 뒤 '입이 화끈거리다'처럼 써요. 비슷한 '후끈'은 공기나 방이 갑자기 더워지는 느낌에 더 어울려요.

phrases.en: I ate something spicy and my mouth is burning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜨거운 느낌이 계속될 때 써요. '화끈'은 갑자기 뜨거워지는 한 순간이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the hot feeling continues, while 화끈 is the sudden moment of heat.

phrases.en: I was embarrassed and my face got hot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부끄럽거나 당황했을 때 얼굴이 뜨거워지는 느낌을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes your face feeling hot from embarrassment.

phrases.en: When I was praised, my ears flushed hot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸의 한 곳이 갑자기 뜨거워질 때 '달아오르다'와 함께 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often paired with '달아오르다' when part of the body suddenly heats up.

explain_en: An onomatopoeic adverb for a part of the body suddenly feeling hot. Used as '얼굴이 화끈거리다' when embarrassed or '입이 화끈거리다' after eating spicy food. The similar '후끈' fits air or a room suddenly turning warm.

examples.en: The two pictures overlap each other by about half.

examples.ko: 두 사진이 겹쳐져서 얼굴이 잘 안 보여요.
examples.en: The two photos overlap, so I can't see the faces well.
I widened the spacing so the letters wouldn't overlap.

examples.ko: 지도 위에 투명 종이를 올리니 선이 겹쳐졌어요.
examples.en: When I put transparent paper over the map, the lines overlapped.

examples.ko: 슬픈 장면에 어머니 모습이 겹쳐져 보였어요.
examples.en: My mother's image seemed to overlap with the sad scene.

examples.ko: 책상 위에서 서류가 겹쳐진 채 쌓여 있어요.
examples.en: The documents are piled up on the desk, overlapping one another.

explain: 일정이나 약속이 겹치는 건 '겹치다'를 써요. '겹쳐지다'는 물건이 저절로 포개지는 모양이나, 두 장면·기억이 마음속에서 포개져 보이는 느낌에 잘 어울려요. 앞에는 '이/가'를 쓰고, 목적어 없이 쓰는 동사예요.

phrases.en: My eyes are tired, so the letters look doubled.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두 모양이 포개져 보일 때 '보이다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 보이다 when two shapes look layered together.

phrases.example: 두 원이 겹쳐진 부분에 색을 칠했어요.
phrases.en: I colored the part where the two circles overlap.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ'을 붙여 이미 포개진 부분을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: The -ㄴ ending points to the part that already overlaps.

phrases.example: 두 도형이 겹쳐지지 않게 놓아 주세요.
phrases.en: Please place the two shapes so they don't overlap.
phrases.nuance_ko: 포개지지 않기를 바랄 때 '-지 않게'로 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used as -지 않게 when you don't want things to overlap.

explain_en: For schedules and appointments clashing, use '겹치다'. '겹쳐지다' fits things that end up stacked on their own, or two scenes and memories that seem to overlap in your mind. It takes a subject with 이/가 and no object.

t90.ax: The two pictures overlap each other by about half.

examples.ko: 두 사건 사이에 관련성이 있는지 조사 중이에요.
examples.en: They are investigating whether the two incidents are related.

examples.ko: 이 연구는 수면과 기억의 관련성을 보여 줘요.
examples.en: This study shows the link between sleep and memory.
Leave out the materials with low relevance and organize the rest.

examples.ko: 질문과 관련성이 없는 대답이라 이해가 안 돼요.
examples.en: The answer has no relevance to the question, so I don't understand it.
I looked into the connection between eating habits and health.

examples.ko: 그 둘의 관련성은 아직 확실하지 않아요.
examples.en: The connection between those two isn't clear yet.

explain: 일상에서는 '관련이 있다/없다'가 더 자주 나오고, '관련성'은 연결의 정도를 말할 때 써서 '관련성이 높다/낮다'처럼 말해요. '관계'는 사람 사이에도 쓰지만 '관련성'은 주로 일, 사건, 자료 사이에 써요.

phrases.example: 이 자료는 우리 주제와 관련성이 높아요.
phrases.en: This material is highly relevant to our topic.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서로 얼마나 이어져 있는지를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say how strongly two things are connected.

phrases.en: The two matters have no connection with each other.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두 일이나 자료가 이어지지 않을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when two events or pieces of data are not connected.

phrases.example: 이 문제는 환경 오염과 관련이 있어요.
phrases.en: This problem is related to environmental pollution.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 '관련성'보다 이 말을 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily speech this is used more often than '관련성'.

explain_en: In daily talk '관련이 있다/없다' is more common, while '관련성' is used when talking about degree, as in '관련성이 높다/낮다'. '관계' can be used between people, but '관련성' is mostly for things, events and materials.

en: to be cute; to be pretty

examples.en: This doll is small and adorable.
My niece came in a cute outfit.
The child waved at me in a charming way.
The cake at that cafe was cute in shape.
The packaging was so cute that I bought it as a gift.
Her way of talking is cute, but she is very sensible inside.

explain: '귀엽다'보다 작고 야무지고 앙증맞은 매력에 써서 큰 동물에는 잘 안 써요. '깜찍한 거짓말'처럼 어린아이의 얄밉고 대담한 행동에 쓰기도 해요. 어른이 귀엽게 행동할 때도 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: That baby outfit is really cute.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작고 앙증맞은 것을 해요체로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this polite form for something small and adorable.

phrases.en: The child told a cheeky little lie.
phrases.nuance_ko: 얄밉지만 귀여운 느낌의 대담한 행동에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for bold behavior that is a little cheeky but endearing.

phrases.en: You look cute in that hat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉으로 보이는 인상을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to describe the impression something gives.

explain_en: Compared with '귀엽다', it fits a small, sharp, dainty charm, so it is rarely used for large animals. It can also describe a cheeky, daring act by a child, as in '깜찍한 거짓말' (a cheeky little lie). It can be used for an adult behaving cutely too.
